description: The identical body inside a `caller()! -> LoadError` declaration. Same call, same `?`, only the enclosing signature differs — so the code keys on the boundary's absence, not on `?` itself.
rationale: §19.5.4 — `?` propagates a failure to the ENCLOSING function's `!` boundary. A function not declared `!` has no such boundary, so there is nowhere for the propagated error to go; the `?` would silently discard a failure mode the callee's type declares. Rejecting it is what keeps the `!` signature an honest summary of a function's failure surface.
